claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 specimens possess a hierarchical heterostructure containing grain boundaries, nanoscale phase distributions, and interfacial regions.
The grain boundaries, nanoscale phases, and interfacial regions in HfNbTiVAl10 can be quantified using pre-test TEM and SEM.

Combining high-resolution static microstructural descriptors with dynamic in situ damage measurements in a multi-fidelity, machine-learning-augmented effective-medium model will predict Young's modulus more accurately than full-field simulations.
The proposed model will predict yield strength more accurately than full-field simulations.
The proposed model will predict fracture-related behavior more accurately than full-field simulations.
The proposed model will produce predictions more rapidly than full-field simulations.
The spatial distribution and connectivity of nanoscale phases, grain boundaries, and interfaces mediate the mechanical response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Dynamic crack-tip evolution and local stress fields provide descriptors relevant to the mechanical response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Correlating static microstructural features and evolving damage indicators with local mechanical responses will allow the model to learn load partitioning.
Correlating static and dynamic descriptors with local responses will allow the model to predict yielding.
Correlating static and dynamic descriptors with local responses will allow the model to predict fracture initiation without full-scale iterative simulations.
The proposed approach will improve predictive accuracy for elastic and plastic parameters by approximately 15–20% relative to conventional full-field simulations.
The proposed approach will reduce computational time by approximately 50% relative to conventional full-field simulations.
Failure to capture key damage mechanisms may cause prediction errors exceeding 30% relative to established simulations.
The model may fail when static or dynamic descriptors do not capture emerging damage mechanisms or scale effects.
The model may fail when temperature or strain rate deviates significantly from the calibration domain.
The targeted accuracy and efficiency improvements are based on theoretical considerations and prior trends in similar systems.
